pairs.why: The two buckets are almost identical: same glossy plastic, same smooth candy and the same weathered, peeling plank floor, so neither is clearly closer to the cleaner real cards.
A's floor shows a little less peeling, scratched wood, so the overall finish is slightly smoother, as the lessons favour.

Both have the same toy-like plastic rendering and the same over-textured worn floor; the only differences are the face design and stripes on B's candy, which don't change how close either is to the real cards.
A's pumpkin is a slightly deeper, more saturated orange and its floor shows a little less peeling paint, which is closer to the clean, bright real cards.
Both have nearly the same finish; B is a bit more vivid but also glossier, and both floors are equally weathered.
A's pumpkin is chunkier, smoother and more saturated, like the bright simple forms of the lawnmower and bumper car, while B is a touch duller.
B's floor has more blue paint flaking and grime, which is the over-textured look the lessons penalise, while A's floor is slightly cleaner.
A has a richer, cleaner orange plastic and a slightly less distressed floor, closer to the smooth, saturated finish of the real cards.
